items.text: Thank you all for reporting bugs and providing feedbackHere’s a handful of fixes and tweaks rolled out with this patch:
Hard Mode Bots: Bots are throwing a bit more of a challenge your way on Hard mode.
Persistent Lobby Countdown: Fixed the countdown showing the wrong time after your first match in a persistent lobby.
First Aid Achievements: Fixed the First Aid achievements not unlocking properly.
Hurricane Truck Localization: Fixed a PT-BR localization issue on Hurricane Truck.
Character Select: Fixed being unable to pick a character after joining a match in progress under “only Graffiti is allowed” rules.
Graffiti’s Ultimate: Fixed Graffiti gaining extra ultimate charge while her ultimate was already active.
Persistent Lobby Symbols: Fixed a bug that blocked lobby creation whenever any type of symbol was used.
Flagassassin Achievement: Fixed players being unable to complete the Flagassassin achievement.
Lobby Description Filter: Added error messaging for persistent lobby descriptions that contain invalid symbols or inappropriate language.
Snowfield: Removed a set of beams inside the barn
See you in the green room!

Update 1.03 is live! Say hello to First Aid, our new dedicated healer, drop into a brand-new map variant, and gather your crew in Persistent Lobbies that stick around match after match. We've also expanded Custom Game Rules, improved the bots, cleaned up the in-match HUD, and added in many fixes based on your reports. Thanks for playing, and keep the feedback coming!

New Contestant: First Aid: Camila’s sister Lucia Barbosa joins the roster as Last Flag's first dedicated healer, complete with a healing rifle, Healing Kit, her robotic pet Oswaldo, and the Ultra Claymore Ultimate.
New Map Variant: A fresh new variant of Copper Falls joins the rotation, ready to play.
Persistent Lobbies: Create a lobby that sticks around match after match. Customize the experience through custom game rules and kick (or ban) anyone that steps out of line.
Lobby Leaderboards: Track who's on top across a Persistent Lobby's matches.
Custom Games Expansion: New rules including a Catch-Up mechanic, Points Victory for Team Deathmatch, Auto Flag Pickup, and rule randomization.
Cleaner Teammate HUD: Teammate nameplates now show class portrait icons instead of plain numbers.
Smarter Bots: Better navigation around jump pads and tubes, plus improved targeting and reliability.
Lots of Fixes: Contestant fixes, map collision and terrain fixes, crash fixes, and UI cleanup.

Meet Lucia Barbosa, call sign First Aid: Last Flag’s first dedicated healer. Where the rest of the cast is built to take ground, First Aid is built to keep your team standing. Her Viral Rifle will heal or damage depending on the target without you needing to think too hard about it. She can place down healing kits for her team or have Oswaldo watch over them and if all else fails there’s always dropping the Ultra Claymore in the middle of the action and letting it do the rest..
Viral Rifle (Base Weapon): Lucia delivers a dose of healing, or damage, depending on the target. Fire and forget and let the tech do the rest as it identifies friend from foe.
Slow Goop (Alt Fire): Lucia’s alt fire creates a puddle of sludge that slows down enemies moving through it.
Healing Kit (Ability): Deploy a Healing Kit to top up the team.
Healing Buddy (Ability): Use Oswaldo, your healing robot, on yourself or on an ally and watch as he heals any damage taken.
Ultra Claymore (Ultimate): When all else fails drop kick this device that rotates on itself rapidly showing the area with the same shots as Lucia’s Viral .
Get Up (Passive): Lucia resurrects allies 25% faster.
Skins: First Aid launches with a full set of skins to unlock, including Hazmat and Sleepover looks.
Executes: Her own Executes, including the Hurricane Truck.
Player Icons: New First Aid player icons
Achievements: Unlock skins and executes by completing her achievements.

With Custom Game Rules, who wants to have to rebuild your lobby each time! Persistent Lobbies maintain the rules you’ve set up so your crew can keep playing without rebuilding the room each time. The lobby owner runs the show: set the rules, manage the leaderboard, and keep matches rolling on a loop. If you don’t like something just update the setup without needing to redo it all.
Stick Around: A Persistent Lobby keeps going match after match instead of dissolving when a match ends.
Owner Controls: The owner can kick, ban, and unban players, including from outside an active match, and can transfer ownership to someone else.
Auto-Restart: Instead of a manual Start, Persistent Lobbies run on a countdown so the next match kicks off automatically.
Rules On The Fly: The owner can update the rules to apply on the next match start.
Lobby Browser: Browse Persistent Lobbies with descriptions and game-mode filters to find a room that fits how you want to play.
Climb The Board: Persistent Lobbies now track a leaderboard so you can see who's leading across the room's matches.
Owner Reset: The lobby owner chooses how often a leaderboard resets..

notes.title: New Map Copper Falls Variant X

items.text: The production team has taken Copper Falls and added a large number of structures, jump pads and power up locations to create Variant X, a map guaranteed to add more mayhem to the action.
We've kept expanding Custom Games with new rules and quality-of-life improvements.
Catch-Up Mechanic: A new Team Deathmatch Catch-Up rule to help trailing teams get back in it, with an in-match indicator so you can see when it's active.

New Win Conditions: Team Deathmatch can now be set to end on a points target and Capture the flag can now have multiple flag caps as a win condition. For capture the flag after scoring the first time the flag is automatically hidden in a new location and the minimap reset.
Auto Flag Pickup: An Auto Flag Pickup rule for Team Deathmatch.
Kill To Heal: A new Kill to Heal custom rule.
Rule Randomizer: Randomize your Custom Game Rules, including custom and weighted randomization for more control over the chaos.
UI Cleanup: Various quality of life improvements make navigating the custom game rules menu more user friendly.
Shield Durability: Fixed Roadie's maxed-out E shield only tanking a single hit.
Ultimate Lockout: Fixed a case where using Roadie's Ultimate and immediately attacking could prevent him from attacking.
Launcher Tuning: Lowered the launcher's damage and gave it a 2x Cashbot multiplier.
Invisibility: Fixed Knives' invisibility cancelling immediately after an attack.
Stealth & Emotes: Stealth no longer cancels when you dance; emoting now cancels crouch instead.
Shield Interaction: Fixed Knives' Dash bypassing Roadie's shield and damaging his health directly.
Portal Prompt: Fixed the Portal dismantle prompt appearing when summoning with Knives.
Stealth Pickup: Fixed the Stealth power-up not working when picked up while disguised.
True Form & Flags: Fixed True Form cancelling when interacting with a Personal Flag.
Falcon Eye Downed: Fixed Scout being unable to move after being downed while using Falcon Eye.
Grand Slam Damage: Fixed incorrect damage calculation for Grand Slam when the target is airborne.
Tornado Visuals: Fixed an upgraded Tornado causing visual corruption after teleportation.
Minigun Targeting: Changed Minigun targeting logic to hitscan.
Victory Pose: Fixed the 'Akanbe' victory pose using the wrong bow animation and getting stuck in a crouched aim pose.
Here's a summary of some of the bugs that were fixed and general improvements that were added. It's not an exhaustive list, there's only so much the cashbots can tabulate before their heads explode.
Team Deathmatch
Personal Flag Polish: Fixed the stretched, misaligned logo on the back of the Personal Flag, and added a dedicated Personal Flag sound.
Capture the Flag
Flag Scored Sound: Added a 'flag scored' sound for matches where more flags are in play.
Custom Games
Match Setup: Fixed being unable to create a custom match with Tango as the only bot, a redundant respawn with the Random Hero rule, and movement issues tied to the 'random on respawn' rule.
In-Match HUD
Teammate Portraits: Teammate nameplates and in-world icons now show a class portrait for each player instead of a plain number, with team coloring applied.
Activity Feed: Cleaned up confusing activity-feed messages into clear, simple callouts (for example, 'player downed').
DBNO Health Bar: Fixed the downed player's HP bar displaying inconsistently.
Menus
Recent Players: Fixed the Recent Players list briefly showing the wrong usernames before updating.
Discord Button: Fixed the Discord button showing in the main menu.
Customization Tab: The 'Mark all as seen' button is now disabled when there are no unseen Customization or Player Icon.
Progression
Level-Up Screen: Fixed the wrong next level being shown on the level-up progress screen.
Rewards Animation: Added an intro XP animation pass to the Rewards screen.
Power-Ups
Jump Pad Shields: Fixed the Shield power-up increasing jump height on vertical jump pads.
Map Pinging
Stray Ping: Fixed pressing '8' on the keyboard pinging a random spot on the map.
Team Deathmatch Starts: Bots no longer try to move into the tubes before a Team Deathmatch match starts.
Smarter Targeting: Bots now prioritize hitting players even when those players aren't carrying flags.
Unstuck: Fixed an AI Contestant getting stuck on a roof, plus general navigation improvements.
Thank you for being part of Last Flag. Have fun out there, and we will see you on the set!

Welcome to Last Flag's latest update which puts you in the showrunner's chair by adding Custom Games, a brand-new Team Deathmatch mode, sharpens the bots, refreshes in-match hit feedback, hands out a fresh Pirate look for every Contestant, and rolls in hundreds of fixes from your feedback. Thanks for playing, and keep the reports coming!
Custom Games: Set your own rules! Give Contestants big heads, lower health, lower respawn time and so much more! Play matches exactly how you want them.
New Mode - Team Deathmatch: Downed enemies drop personal flags that can be scored at friendly radar towers and pyramids. No team flag hiding or searching, just action packed mayhem.
Hit Feedback Refresh: Redesigned directional damage indicators and cleaner, clearer hit ticks.

Reward Screen: New Reward screen which lets you track all the cosmetics you can unlock as well as a new leveling celebration at the end of a match make it easier to see all the cool things you can unlock for free.
Smarter Bots: Better flag interception, smarter revives, and improved navigation.
Pirate Skins: Every Contestant now has a new Pirate-themed skin to unlock.
Lots of Bug Fixes: Map collision passes, Contestant polish, UI cleanup, localization, stability improvements, etc..

You're the showrunner now. Custom Games lets you bend the rules of Last Flag to your liking, change values, turn rules on or off completely, to craft the perfect combination. Want a frantic 10-minute sprint with Big Heads and Infinite Ammo? A slow, tactical fight with beefed-up health and no power-ups? It's your show.
Here are some (but not all) of the settings you will be able to adjust.
Adjust match length (10 to 60 minutes), respawn time, and whether Overtime is enabled (including how long the Overtime flag defense lasts).
Decide whether players can use abilities or keep their stamina while carrying the flag, choose the Flag Hiding mode (Player Hide, Auto-Hide, or off), and tune the Flag Hiding phase duration.

Enable or disable individual Contestants, or finally allow duplicates per team. Fine-tune global and per-Contestant Health, Damage, Ultimate charge rate, and ability upgrade costs, or start everyone with upgraded abilities.

Turn power-ups on or off, set their respawn rate and duration, or mask what power-up you will get until you pick it up - everyone loves surprises. Toggle Gold and Red Cashbots, and even change Cashbot size.
Tune Radar Tower capture rate, healing rate, and reveal speed.
Flip on the fun stuff: Big Heads, Infinite Ammo, and a Down But Not Dead toggle.

NOTE: Last Flag productions is not responsible for whatever happens when you combine all these rules. Some combinations may not be the best fit for each other and make the game behave weirdly. Use with caution (or maybe not).

Team Deathmatch shakes up the formula with Personal Flags. Instead of one shared team flag, eliminated opponents drop Personal Flags that you scoop up and deliver to a Radar Towers you control or to your Pyramid to score.
Personal Flags: Collect dropped Personal Flags and deliver them to a Radar Tower you control or to your Pyramid to score. Return an ally’s flag before the enemy can score it to also earn points.
Carry Limits: You can carry up to 5 Personal flags at once..
New HUD: A dedicated Team Deathmatch HUD shows your Personal Flag count, delivery feedback, a phase timer, and nameplates for dropped flags (including a despawn timer).
We reworked in-match hit feedback so it's clearer what's happening to you in a fight.
Directional Damage Indicators: Moved farther from the center of the screen so they're easier to read at a glance and clutter the action less.
Hit Ticks: Simplified and now sit on the outside of the crosshair and no longer animate inward.
Downed Clarity: Omni-directional damage indicators are now disabled while taking damage ticks during DBNO, so they're no longer confused with real incoming damage.
Turret Color: Arsenal's Tesla Turret no longer changes color after being launched by a jump pad.
Turret Deploy: The turret asset no longer bounces when deploying.
Reload Animation: Fixed the reload animation missing the latest canister, which made the weapon appear to float.
Tornado Sound: The Tornado throw sound now plays from Arsenal rather than from the projectile's spawn point.
Model Fix: Banshee's model no longer bends unnaturally.
Weapon Spread: Reduced how much movement speed affects her weapon's spread.
Disguise & Flag: Graffiti can no longer open the Master of Disguise wheel while carrying the flag.
Stealth & Flag: Knives no longer cancels stealth when holding the flag.
Shield From Behind: Fixed interactions when shooting Roadie from behind while his Shield is open.
MVP Rifle: Scout's rifle now correctly appears in his MVP animation.
Land Mine Prop: Fixed the Land Mine prop being missing during its animation.
Player Bots
Flag Interception: Bots are now better at intercepting flag carriers.
Smarter Revives: Improved how bots decide whether to revive a teammate.
Navigation: Bots no longer try to use launchpads during the hide-the-flag phase, and got general fixes for getting stuck.
Cosmetics & Progression
Set Sail: Every Contestant now has a new Pirate-themed skin available to unlock.
Rewards Screen: Implemented the new post-match Rewards screen and Rewards Tab, with updated art and animation, a button to skip the animation, and faster XP rollup.
Percentage Fields: Fixed percentage values that couldn't be applied manually and could break when very large numbers were entered.
Contestant Selection: Fixed the Contestant selection bar breaking when a Contestant was disabled, and the case where all Contestants could be disabled at once.
Ukrainian Chat: Fixed chat names not being highlighted in Ukrainian.
Out of Bounds: Numerous out-of-bounds, missing-collision, and stuck-spot fixes across Copper Falls, Snowfield, and Twin Temples.
Thank you for being part of Last Flag. Have fun out there, and we will see you on the set!
Joining the contestant cast: Graffiti

She's got wheels, she's got paint, and she's got SHOWTIME written all over her. Meet Stella Wylde, aka Graffiti, the tenth contestant to join the Last Flag roster, and Fex Television's boldest signing yet.

On skates and armed with a can of spray paint, Graffiti rewrites the rules of the game in real time. Whether she's circling opponents on the field or tagging them with her signature moves, she's must-watch television.
Welcome to the Twin Temples

Fex Television spared no expense unearthing this one. Hidden deep in the jungle, the Twin Temples have been restored to their glory, and their secrets, just for you. Explore them before anyone else does.
Tight corridors, an exposed bridge, and the ruins of a long-lost civilization, Twin Temples is a flag-runner's nightmare and a defender's dream. Hold your breath. Both teams are coming.
Brand new sportswear

Rep your home field and look the part doing it. The new jersey-themed cosmetic collection lets you suit up in your team's colors, flex your style on the battleground, and finish your opponents in spectacular fashion—local allegiance never looked so good.
If you're newer to Last Flag, here's a quick reference for the terms and shorthand used throughout these notes:
Contestant: Any of the playable characters on the Last Flag roster.
Q / E / C: The default hotkeys for a Contestant's three abilities. Q is the first ability, E is the second, and C is the Ultimate.
Alt-Fire: A secondary action on a Contestant's primary weapon, mapped to right mouse button by default.
Ultimate: A Contestant's most powerful ability (the C key). Charges up over the course of a match as the player deals damage and completes objectives.
Charge: How full a Contestant's Ultimate ability is. Shown as a percentage on the ability icon until full.
Down But Not Out (DBNO): The state a Contestant enters after losing all their health. While downed, an ally can revive you. If left alone, you bleed out and respawn.
Finisher: A short animation that plays when you eliminate a downed Contestant.
MVP: The Most Valuable Player from each match. The MVP gets a spotlight pose during the post-match screens.
Cashbots: The robots that wander the map. Destroy them for in-match currency you can spend on ability upgrades.
Green Room: Last Flag's waiting area, where players go before matches, upon respawn, and after being eliminated.
Introducing Graffiti: The newest Contestant skates onto the set, armed with twin paintball pistols, a devastating "Star Form" ultimate, and a knack for blending in.
Welcome to Twin Temples: A brand-new map enters rotation: a stone arena split between sun-soaked bright side and shadow-cloaked dark side.
Smarter Bots: Player Bots have received a major behavioral pass with improved pathing, ability use, and decision-making.
Streamer Mode: A new privacy setting in Game Settings that hides sensitive info from your overlay.
Audio Mixing Pass: A wide-ranging mixing pass to prioritize important gameplay sounds, plus brand-new hit and damage SFX.
Hundreds of Fixes: Tuning, audio polish, art polish, localization, bug fixes, and stability improvements across the entire game.

There's a new artist on the set of Last Flag, and she's painting the town red, blue, yellow, and every color in between. Graffiti glides into the arena on a pair of custom roller skates, twin paintball pistols at the ready, with a talent for blending in when she'd rather not be seen. Whether she's covering the competition with splashes of paint or vanishing into the scenery, expect a colorful debut that the audience won't soon forget.
Dual-wielded paintball pistols that splash paint on impact, aim for the head to cover your target's view and disrupt them in the heat of the moment.
Sprint Cancellation: Sprint is no longer cancelled by Dash Stab or Dive Roll attacks that don't connect with a target.
Sprint & Jump Pads: Sprint is no longer cancelled when using a jump pad. You'll keep your momentum when you land.

Down But Not Dead: Fixed a bug where waiting in DBNO would lead to a longer respawn time. Now whether you wait until the end of DBNO, give up early or are killed your respawn time is the same (15 seconds).
Hit Impact Visuals: Decreased the visual size of hit impact effects. The previous size was overwhelming and made it hard to see what was happening in fights.
Flag Interactions: Fixed an issue where you could be automatically downed immediately after returning the flag.
Flag Interactions: If a player disconnected mid-flag-interaction, the flag could become unusable for about a minute. The lockout window has been substantially shortened.
Power-Up Stations: Projectiles and abilities (such as Tango's Proximity Mines) no longer pass through Power-Up stations.
Cashbot Spawning: Fixed an infrequent issue where Cashbots would spawn too closely rather than distributed across the map.

Smarter Player Bots: Bots now have significantly improved pathing, stuck movement recovery, and decision-making. They are also smarter about hunting for the flag, defending the pyramid, and choosing when to use their abilities.
Brass Belcher Minigun (C)
Cancel Animation: The Minigun no longer visually distorts when cancelling the Ultimate.
Shotguns (Primary)
Reload: Shotguns no longer occasionally fail to fully reload when triggered.
Sprint: Sprint no longer breaks when jumping mid-fall.
Dash Stab (Q)
Sound: Dash Stab sound now plays at the correct location.
Interrupt Restored: Hits with Dash Stab once again interrupt the target.
Going Dark (E)
Teleport Fix: Going Dark could fail to activate if Knives had just been teleported by Arsenal's Q.E.R. This has been resolved.
Melee Alignment: Lumberjack's melee attacks were drifting out of alignment with his swing animations. They now connect where you'd expect.
Animation Hitches: Addressed jump hitches.
Stealth Interactions
Visibility Fix: Skyfire's VFX particles no longer appear while he is in Stealth, which previously gave his position away to enemies.
Shield (Alt-Fire)
Stun on Break: When Roadie's Shield breaks, he is now stunned in place rather than knocked back. This comes with accompanying balance changes for Shield uptime.
Open/Close Audio: The Shield open sound no longer persists after the Shield has closed.
Server/Client Sync: Roadie's projectiles could explode on the server but appear to bounce off on the client. This desync has been fixed.
Scout Ultimate: Roadie now correctly takes damage from Scout's Ultimate while his Shield is open. He was unintentionally invulnerable to it before.
Inspired Riff (E)
Upgrade Radius: Fixed a bug where the Inspired Riff radius incorrectly grew when the radio was upgraded.
Snowfield Rooftops: Inspired Riff can now be placed on the roof of certain Snowfield buildings, where it previously could not be placed.
Redeemer Joyride (C)
Lean Animations: Lean animations correctly play again during Joyride.
We performed a wide-ranging mixing pass to make sure important gameplay audio cues come through more clearly when there's a lot going on. Your ears will thank you.
Performed an HDR mixing pass prioritizing feedback sounds during combat.
Hit Tick Volume: Hit ticks were too loud and dominating other audio cues. They have been brought down to a more reasonable level.
Critical Hit SFX: Implemented a new distinct sound effect for critical hits, so you immediately know when you've landed a meaningful shot.
Receiving Damage SFX: Designed and implemented a new version of the SFX that plays when you take damage so it's easier to quickly know the location of a firing enemy.
Knives: Dash Stab sound now plays at the correct location. Previously it could play silently or at world origin (which sounded silent to most players).
Flag Capture Loop: Fixed an endless looping Last Flag sound effect that could persist when the capture ended.
Black Icons Fix: Fixed an issue where player icons on the minimap could appear solid black.
Green Room Visibility: Scout and Tango no longer incorrectly appear on the minimap while in the Green Room.
Twin Temples Minimap: Added the dedicated background art for the Twin Temples minimap.
Bounty Hunter Ammo: Bounty Hunter's ammo count is no longer displayed as a progress bar; it shows numerically again.
Tango Bolas UI: Tango's Bolas UI effect no longer displays while the player is downed.
Reticle Visibility: Increased the opacity of reticle outlines so they're easier to see against busy backgrounds.
Player Names: Player names in Team Selection are no longer force-uppercased.
Leaderboard Nicknames: Nicknames now appear correctly on the in-game Leaderboard.
Bug Report Button: The Bug Report button no longer flickers when hovering over its left edge.

UI Overlap Fixes: Addressed multiple cases where UI buttons were overlapping or being overlapped by the chat box in Mexican Spanish, Italian, German, Ukrainian, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, and Indonesian.
Activity Feed: Fixed previously untranslated Activity Feed for Mexican Spanish.
Friend Invite Crash: Fixed a crash that could occur after sending a friend invite.
Achievement-Get Crash: Fixed a rare crash that could occur during engine shutdown after achievements had been awarded in a match.
Friend-Result Crash: Fixed a rare crash related to receiving friend list updates.
Thanks for the support, feedback, ideas, and general good vibes. Happy flag hunting and see you on the set.
We’ve just released a small update so that we can apply a few new bug fixes.
Matchmaking: Made improvements to reduce cases where players could be matched into games on incorrect servers, which resulted in higher than expected in-game ping.
Roadie: Shield now correctly protects against melee damage and Skyfire’s flamethrower.
Exploits: Patched up a pair of locations in Copper Falls that could allow a player to get outside the boundaries of the map.
Stability: Addressed a client crash that could occur for players using certain Intel 13th and 14th gen CPUs.

Today, we’re releasing a small update for Last Flag that includes a few big changes, like the addition of an Oceania server, a change that lets you swipe your preferred contestant from a bot, a few balance changes, and a round of bug fixes. We have many more changes incoming, but wanted to get these out to you as quickly as possible. Catch the details below.

We’ve been hearing from a number of our friends in Oceania that they would prefer to have a server that’s closer to home, rather than connecting to Asia. And so, with today’s patch we’ve added an Oceania server option to the game.
The best way to anchor a match to the Oceania server will be to create your own lobby:
Go to the Play menu, and then select Lobbies.
Press the Create button
Change the “Region” dropdown to **Oceania** and then press “Create.”
Contestant Selection: Players can now select a contestant that is currently in use by a bot, which means no bots monopolizing the contestants you want to play is a thing of the past.
This might mean that two of the same contestant may appear on the same team until the bot dies and swaps contestants.

Flag Handling: Bots will no longer attempt to pick up an enemy flag as long as there human players on the team. However, bots will still attempt to return friendly flags (whether dropped by an enemy or in the pyramid during the defense countdown.

More to come: In addition to the changes above, we are also reading feedback from the community on areas where bot behavior could be improved. We’re actively working on a list of improvements for a future patch that will help make them better teammates.

With this update we’re making tuning changes to several contestants. These changes were ready to go, which is why they are in this patch but we are actively working on other balance adjustments. We are also keeping a close eye on community feedback, as well as our internal data for the entire cast. Please keep it coming! Feel free to drop us a note on balance any time in the Last Flag Discord.
Shotguns (Primary Weapon)
Julius has been working on his Shotguns. He cleaned out the barrels so they’ll shoot a bit farther and be a bit more effective in his midrange.
He’s also swapped in a new magazine so he can fire 6 rounds before reloading.

You spoke, and we’re listening. Knives has been tuned down in response to player feedback that she just wasn't fun to fight against. She no longer does additional damage when attacking out of Stealth.

While we loved seeing her have a variation of the classic "Back Stab" move often seen in Rogue type characters, we felt that this mechanic was giving her too much of an edge when sneaking up on targets, especially when Going Dark can be triggered in combat for an instant damage boost to your next attack. Don't worry, you can still access Stealth with the same mechanics as before, and attack from the shadows to surprise your targets with rapid damage, just not as much rapid damage that really made her too strong.
Stealth (Passive & Going Dark)
Soo-Jin no longer receives a damage bonus when attacking from Stealth.
Axe Throw (Alt-Fire)
After spending the afternoon sharpening his axes, Peter’s Axe Throw will now break Roadie’s Shield on pullback.
Forest Wrath (Ultimate)
Peter has added a few leg day sessions to his workout routine, and he now moves faster during his big leap while using Forest Wrath. This will help him close in on targets while in ultimate form.
Electrified Bolas (Q)

Alejandro’s Bolas are now more… stunning. He’s modified them to increase the Stun duration from 0.5 seconds to 1.5 seconds. His tinkering isn’t perfect, though, because the Stun will break if his target takes any damage.
Bunker Buster Bazooka (Ultimate)
Speaking of tinkering, Alejandro’s fortified his boots to be more blast resistant. As a result he’ll now take 50% less self-inflicted damage if he steps too close to his own Bazooka’s explosions.
Connectivity: Addressed an issue that could cause players to receive a “Game Server Disconnected” error message when trying to join a match.
Exploits: Addressed a few locations on Copper Falls and Snowfield that could allow a player to get outside the boundaries of the map.
Flag Hiding: Removed several flag hiding spots on Copper Falls and Snowfield that were too difficult for most contestants to reach.
Announcer: Clay loves his job so much that sometimes he’d keep up the commentary all the way through the victory screen. Going forward, we’re muting his mic as soon as the match ends.

items.text: We’ve just released a small patch to address the following issues discovered during launch week:
Copper Falls: Hiding the flag in certain locations very near the dividing curtain no longer prevents Radar Towers from revealing the flag.
Server Stability: Fixed a rare issue that could result in a server crash during gameplay.

Please note: Thank you very much for reporting bugs you've encountered using the in-game Bug Report Tool (Gameplay Settings -> Enable Bug Report), as well as in our Discord server, on forums, and elsewhere. We are actively investigating and working on fixes for the issues you've reported so far. Keep an eye out for additional patches with additional fixes in the near future.
